newsitem.title: UK: UK receiverships up 3.9 percent in Q3 '96 - survey.
newsitem.headline: UK receiverships up 3.9 percent in Q3 '96 - survey.

text.p: UK business receiverships in the third quarter of 1996 were 3.9 percent higher in number than those seen in the previous three months, according to a survey from accountants KPMG.
But the number of British companies that failed in Q3 was 16.6 percent below the total seen in the same quarter last year.
KPMG recorded 347 receiverships in the last quarter, up from the 334 seen in the second quarter but well below the 416 in Q3 1995.
"Compared with the early 1990s, we are now seeing a very much lower number of receiverships," Mike Wheeler, KPMG's head of corporate recovery, said on Wednesday.
He said companies failing now were doing so for reasons such as poor management, inadequate funding or an inability to adapt -- not because of recession.
"There is strong evidence that consumer confidence is returning and companies, if they are to survive and grow, must ensure that they are able to capitalise on this," Wheeler said.
